description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problem categories from the MathOdyssey dataset, classified by subject and difficulty level. The chart is divided into 12 distinct slices, which do not appear to be ordered by size. There is no separate legend and no percentage labels inside the slices; instead, each segment is identified by an external label connected via a thin grey line, detailing the category name, percentage, and raw count in parentheses. None of the segments are visually emphasized through explosion or offset. Starting from the top left and moving clockwise, the largest slice is dark blue, representing "Algebra – Olympiad-level" at 21.19% (82). This is followed by a light blue slice for "Statistics – University-level" at 4.39% (17), a cyan slice for "Probability – University-level" at 5.43% (21), an olive green slice for "Differential Equations – University-level" at 3.62% (14), a grey slice for "Calculus and Analysis – University-level" at 6.20% (24), and a pink slice for "Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level" at 6.46% (25). Continuing clockwise, a brown slice denotes "Pre-Calculus – High School" at 14.21% (55), a light purple slice shows "Geometry – High School" at 3.62% (14), a salmon-colored slice represents "Algebra – High School" at 17.83% (69), a light green slice indicates "Combinatorics – Olympiad-level" at 9.56% (37), and an orange slice corresponds to "Geometry – Olympiad-level" at 6.46% (25). Finally, a very thin, pale blue slice is labeled with a greyed-out obscured box followed by "– Olympiad-level" at 1.03% (4).
